title: Canonical affine charts give a quasi-compact open immersion
statement: Let $X,Y,S$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $f:X\to S$ and $\pi:Y\to S$ be morphisms, and let $c:X\to Y$ satisfy $\pi\circ c=f$. Assume that $\pi$ is affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]. For every affine open $U\subseteq S$, write $X_U=f^{-1}(U)$, $Y_U=\pi^{-1}(U)$ and let $c_U:X_U\to Y_U$ be the restriction of $c$. Assume that $X_U$ is quasi-affine, meaning isomorphic to a quasi-compact open subscheme of an affine scheme (quasi-compact means that every open covering has a finite subcover). Suppose that for each such $U$ there is an isomorphism $h_U:Y_U\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(X_U,\mathcal O_{X_U})$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with $h_U\circ c_U=j_{X_U}$, where $j_{X_U}$ is the morphism corresponding to the identity of $\Gamma(X_U,\mathcal O_{X_U})$ under [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. Then $c$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] and is quasi-compact as a morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. No quasi-compactness or separation hypothesis on $S$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 01SM, lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, proof (2) implies (4), final two sentences: canonical affine restrictions are quasi-compact open immersions, and so is can

proof.text: Choose an affine open cover $S=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$ and put $W_i=f^{-1}(U_i)$ and $V_i=\pi^{-1}(U_i)$. Inverse images of open sets are open, so the $W_i$ cover $X$ and the $V_i$ cover $Y$. Each $V_i$ is affine by the definition of the affine morphism $\pi$. The equality $\pi\circ c=f$ gives $c^{-1}(V_i)=W_i$: a point $x$ belongs to the left side exactly when $\pi(c(x))=f(x)$ belongs to $U_i$. Thus $c_i:W_i\to V_i$ is exactly the restriction of $c$ over the target open $V_i$.

source.place: Tag 01SM, lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, proof (2) implies (4), final two sentences

proof.text: For each $i$, the hypothesis makes $W_i$ a quasi-affine scheme. Apply [lem-trf-quasi-affine-canonical-affine-embedding] to $W_i$: it is quasi-compact and its canonical map $j_i:W_i\to\operatorname{Spec}\Gamma(W_i,\mathcal O_{W_i})$ is an open immersion. The given identity $h_i\circ c_i=j_i$ and the inverse of the isomorphism $h_i$ yield $c_i=h_i^{-1}\circ j_i$. In the definition of open immersion, an isomorphism identifies the open image and its restricted structure sheaf with their images under that isomorphism. Consequently $c_i$ is an open immersion and hence injective on points.

source.place: Tag 01P9, lemma-quasi-affine, forward implication; applied as in Tag 01SM, proof (2) implies (4)

proof.text: To check injectivity of $c$, suppose $c(x)=c(x\prime)$. Then $f(x)=\pi(c(x))=\pi(c(x\prime))=f(x\prime)$. Choose $U_i$ containing this common point of $S$. Both $x$ and $x\prime$ belong to $W_i$, and injectivity of $c_i$ gives $x=x\prime$. For every $x\in X$ some $W_i$ contains $x$. Its inclusion $W_i\hookrightarrow X$ is an open immersion, and its composite with $c$ is the open immersion $c_i$ followed by $V_i\hookrightarrow Y$. This composite is an open immersion directly from the definition: an open subset of the open subset $V_i$ is open in $Y$, and restriction of $\mathcal O_Y$ first to $V_i$ and then to that subset is its direct restriction. Thus all hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-injective-local-source] hold for $c$. That node gives that $c$ is an open immersion.

source.place: Tag 01SM, lemma-characterize-quasi-affine, proof (2) implies (4), final two sentences

proof.text: Each $V_i$ is affine, so [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs] makes it quasi-separated. The source $W_i$ is quasi-compact by step 2. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence], applied with source $W_i$, target $V_i$ and morphism $c_i$, therefore gives that $c_i$ is quasi-compact. The quasi-separatedness required here belongs to the affine chart $V_i$; no separation hypothesis on $S$ or $Y$ is used.

source.place: Tag 03GI, lemma-quasi-compact-permanence, applied over Spec Z; Tag 01KN, lemma-affine-separated; as used for the chart quasi-compactness in Tag 01SM

proof.text: The opens $V_i$ cover $Y$ and $c^{-1}(V_i)=W_i$ by step 1, so step 4 proves quasi-compactness of every target restriction $c^{-1}(V_i)\to V_i$. Apply [lem-pc-quasi-compact-local-on-target] to this open cover to conclude that $c$ is quasi-compact. Together with step 3 this proves both assertions. This locality theorem allows an arbitrary open cover; we have taken no finite subcover of $S$ or $Y$.
